title: The Pale Harvest
premise: Quentin Dravenmoor, a property surveyor, is hired to appraise Hollowmere House, a decaying estate whose previous owners all vanished within a year of purchase. When an excavation crew unearths a stone door sealed from the inside, Quentin discovers the house has been appraising them in return—cataloguing their memories, their griefs, their debts. The door was sealed by the last heir to keep something fed and contained, but the seal is failing, and the well beneath the house is refilling with everything it has swallowed. To survive until sunrise, Quentin must learn what was invited in generations ago and choose whether to inherit the debt or pay it forward.
about_author: Rafael Vane spent a decade as a rural land assessor before turning to horror fiction, drawing on the strange silences of unclaimed properties. They live off-grid in the northern hills, where they insist every old house deserves a fair hearing.

chapters.title: The Commission
chapters.summary: Quentin accepts the appraisal job at Hollowmere House despite its reputation for swallowing owners whole. Third-person limited POV establishes their pragmatism and buried guilt over a family estate they sold out from under their dying mother. Emotional beat: uneasy ambition masking avoidance.

chapters.title: Square Footage
chapters.summary: First walkthrough. Rooms measure differently on each pass; a hallway is four feet longer than the blueprints allow. Quentin logs it as settling foundations. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: professional denial beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Previous Owners
chapters.summary: In the county archive, Quentin finds a pattern: every owner since 1891 filed identical complaints—heavy footsteps above the attic, water sounds below the cellar—then disappeared. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Excavation
chapters.summary: The crew digging the drainage trench strikes stone: a door, iron-banded, sealed from the inside with molten lead poured through a slot. The foreman jokes about it; his laugh dies when the ground hums. POV: alternating Quentin and foreman Dara Okafor. Emotional beat: collective unease.

chapters.title: What the House Knows
chapters.summary: That night Quentin dreams the house's memories: a wedding, a funeral, a bargain struck over an open well. They wake with mud on their feet though they never left bed. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: violation—the house has begun reading them back.

chapters.title: Dara's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dara reveals her crew has been losing hours—whole afternoons gone, tools found arranged in patterns no one made. She shows Quentin her grandfather's notebook; he surveyed this land in 1962 and wrote one repeated line: IT COUNTS WHAT YOU CARRY. POV: Dara. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Well Refills
chapters.summary: Water rises in the dry cellar well overnight, warm and tasting of iron and old rain. Quentin realizes the disappearances coincide with the well brimming. Something below is surfacing. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: the abstract threat becomes physical.

chapters.title: Invited In
chapters.summary: In the parish records Quentin finds the original deed's covenant: the first Dravenmoor-adjacent family invited 'a keeper' into the well to protect their harvests—and agreed to feed it memory in exchange. Every heir since has paid. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: horrified recognition of inheritance as contract.

chapters.title: The Attic Counts
chapters.summary: The footsteps above the attic grow rhythmic, deliberate—counting. Quentin counts back and realizes the number matches people who have died on the property. One more than yesterday. POV: Dara. Emotional beat: terror of being tallied.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: Quentin examines the unearthed door and understands: someone locked themselves IN with the thing, not out. Scratched into the stone: the last heir's name and date—three years ago. The seal is failing because the keeper inside is starving. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: grief reframed as sacrifice.

chapters.title: What Was Invited
chapters.summary: Through the house's borrowed memories, Quentin sees the keeper's true nature: not a demon but a hunger given purpose, fed on recollection so the town could forget its own cruelties. The town's peace was purchased with amnesia. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: moral vertigo—power corrupting even memory itself.

chapters.title: Dara Disappears
chapters.summary: Dara goes to retrieve her crew's equipment alone and doesn't return. Her radio plays back her own voice counting, slower and slower. Quentin finds her boots at the well's edge, dry. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: loss weaponized—the house takes what Quentin carries.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: The house manifests its assessment of Quentin: rooms filled with their mother's voice, the sale papers, the hospital corridor they fled. It offers a trade—forget her death, forget the guilt, stay forever comfortable. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: temptation rendered intimate.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Quentin refuses the comfort, choosing to keep the pain because it's theirs. The house recoils; doors slam; the temperature drops. The keeper below stirs, interested in resistance. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: defiance as identity.

chapters.title: Below
chapters.summary: Quentin descends through the cellar as the well overflows, wading into rising water toward the sealed door. The dead of Hollowmere stand in the flood, mouths moving, returning what was taken from them. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: courage built from grief.

chapters.title: The Last Heir
chapters.summary: At the door Quentin meets the remnant of the heir who sealed herself in three years ago—Dara's missing crew among her ranks now. She explains the terms: the well refills at dawn unless someone takes up the keeping willingly. POV: Quentin with the heir's interludes. Emotional beat: communion with the sacrificed.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: The heir offers Quentin the choice: take the burden, destroy the door and flood the town's forgetting back into the world, or walk away and let the well choose its next keeper. Power, she warns, always rewrites whoever holds it. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: the thematic crux—inheriting versus ending.

chapters.title: Sunrise Clause
chapters.summary: Hours before dawn, Quentin works the problem like a surveyor: measuring the covenant, finding the loophole in the deed's language. A keeper must be invited—but nothing says the invitation can't be refused collectively. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: hope through precision.

chapters.title: The Counting Stops
chapters.summary: Quentin returns the stolen memories to the dead, speaking each name aloud, refusing to keep or be kept. The footsteps above falter. The keeper, unfed and unnamed, loses its claim. The house begins to empty itself. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: catharsis through restitution.

chapters.title: Refilling
chapters.summary: The well surges one final time, offering Quentin everything—power, permanence, their mother's voice again. Quentin steps back from the edge and lets it drain. The door cracks along its lead seam. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: climax of renunciation.

chapters.title: Sunrise
chapters.summary: Dawn. The house stands hollowed, rooms finally matching their measurements. Dara emerges from the flood alive but without three years of memory, and chooses not to ask for them back. Quentin files the appraisal: structure unsound, recommend demolition. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: exhausted relief.

chapters.title: Fair Market Value
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Months later, Quentin passes the razed lot where Hollowmere stood; the grass grows pale there, and no birds land. At home, Quentin opens a box of their mother's things and reads her handwriting, remembering on purpose. Somewhere far off, faintly, something begins counting again. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: bittersweet vigilance—inherited memory, freely kept.
